verses.text: The LORD said to Moses,
"Pay back the Midianites for what they did to the people of Israel. After that you will die and join your people."
So Moses said to the people, "Prepare some of your men for war, so they can go against Midian and carry out the LORD's punishment on them.
Send one thousand men from each of the tribes of Israel to fight."
So one thousand men were chosen from each tribe from the many thousands of Israel, twelve thousand men ready for battle.
Moses sent them to war, one thousand from each tribe, along with Phinehas, son of Eleazar the priest. Phinehas took with him things from the holy place and the trumpets for sounding the alarm.
They fought against Midian, as the LORD had commanded Moses, and killed every man.
Among those killed were the five kings of Midian: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba. They also killed Balaam son of Beor with the sword.
The people of Israel captured the Midianite women and children, and took all their cattle, flocks, and goods as plunder.
They burned all the towns where the Midianites lived, and all their camps.
They took all the plunder and everything they had captured, both people and animals.
They brought the captives, the animals, and the plunder to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the community of Israel at their camp on the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan across from Jericho.
Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the leaders of the community went out of the camp to meet them.
Moses was angry with the officers of the army, the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, who had come back from the battle.
He asked them, "Have you let all the women live?
They are the ones who followed Balaam's advice and led the people of Israel to be unfaithful to the LORD in what happened at Peor. That is why the disease struck the LORD's people.
Now kill every boy, and kill every woman who has slept with a man.
But save for yourselves every girl who has never slept with a man.
All of you who have killed anyone or touched a dead body must stay outside the camp for seven days. On the third and seventh days you must make yourselves and your captives clean.
Also make clean every piece of clothing, and everything made of leather, goat hair, or wood."
Then Eleazar the priest said to the soldiers who had gone into battle, "This is the rule from the law that the LORD gave Moses:
Gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin, lead,

and anything else that can stand the heat, must be passed through fire, and then it will be clean. But it must also be made clean with the cleansing water. Whatever cannot stand the heat must be passed through the water.
On the seventh day, wash your clothes, and you will be clean. Then you may come into the camp."
The LORD said to Moses,
"You, Eleazar the priest, and the family leaders of the community must count all the people and animals that were captured.
Divide them into two equal parts: one for the soldiers who went into battle and one for the rest of the community.
From the soldiers' half, set apart a share for the LORD: one out of every five hundred, whether people, cattle, donkeys, or sheep and goats.
Take this from their half and give it to Eleazar the priest as the LORD's special gift.

From the half that belongs to the people of Israel, take one out of every fifty, whether people, cattle, donkeys, sheep and goats, or other animals. Give them to the Levites, who take care of the LORD's Holy Tent."
So Moses and Eleazar the priest did as the LORD commanded Moses.
The plunder left from what the soldiers had taken was six hundred seventy-five thousand sheep and goats,
seventy-two thousand cattle,
sixty-one thousand donkeys,
and thirty-two thousand women who had never slept with a man.
The half that belonged to the soldiers was three hundred thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep and goats,
and the LORD's share of these was six hundred seventy-five.
There were thirty-six thousand cattle, and the LORD's share was seventy-two.
There were thirty thousand five hundred donkeys, and the LORD's share was sixty-one.
There were sixteen thousand people, and the LORD's share was thirty-two.
Moses gave the LORD's share as a special gift to Eleazar the priest, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The other half belonged to the people of Israel, the half that Moses had set apart from the soldiers' share.
The community's half was three hundred thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep and goats,
thirty-six thousand cattle,
thirty thousand five hundred donkeys,
and sixteen thousand people.
From the people of Israel's half, Moses took one out of every fifty people and animals, as the LORD had commanded him. He gave them to the Levites, who took care of the LORD's Holy Tent.
Then the officers over the army units, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, came to Moses.
They said to him, "We, your servants, have counted the soldiers under our command, and not one man is missing.
So we have brought the LORD a gift of the gold jewellery each of us found: arm bands, bracelets, rings, earrings, and necklaces. We bring them to make ourselves right with the LORD."
Moses and Eleazar the priest accepted the gold from them, all of it made into jewellery.
All the gold that the commanders of thousands and of hundreds gave as a special gift to the LORD weighed sixteen thousand seven hundred fifty shekels.
Each of the soldiers had taken plunder for himself.
Moses and Eleazar the priest took the gold from the commanders of thousands and of hundreds and brought it into the Tent of Meeting, so that the LORD would remember the people of Israel.
